primitives.name: Competitive Balance Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: The concept of competitive balance, which refers to a well-balanced distribution of sporting talent across teams, is widely considered fundamental to a league's long-term viability and success (Rottenberg, 1956; Jennett, 1984; Humphreys, 2002).
primitives.assumptions: Teams have latent skill levels; balance is inferred via observed outcomes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( B < 0.3 \), league is considered imbalanced.

layer2.mapping: GSI infers \( B \) via posterior belief over skill variances; GSE models \( B \) as a time-varying state variable.
layer2.telemetry: Points distribution variance and championship probability spread.

primitives.name: Turning Point Coefficient
primitives.verbatim_quote: This work focuses on competitive balance within a tournament season, often called seasonal (or within-season) competitive balance.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\tau': 'expected time of competitive divergence in tournament schedule (unit: match number)'}
primitives.assumptions: Tournament schedule is fixed; \( \tau \) is a deterministic function of match order.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \tau \) is early, perceived balance is low.

layer2.mapping: GSI uses \( \tau \) as a proxy for schedule-induced entropy; GSE uses \( \tau \) to model state transition timing.
layer2.telemetry: Match result entropy and championship probability evolution.
